#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Blog post formatter. The function `format_blog_entry` takes a headline and the body of a blog post, sanitises them for safe HTML rendering and injects them into a pre‑defined template. The implementation follows the following security principles: * Input validation – only strings are accepted. * Output escaping – all HTML special characters are escaped to avoid injection of malicious markup or scripts. * Structured output – the resulting string always contains the same well‑formed HTML skeleton, protecting against malformed or partial responses (CWE‑707). """ import html # Predefined HTML structure with placeholders for title and body BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def format_blog_entry(headline: str, content: str) -> str: """ Prepare a blog post for web display. Parameters ---------- headline : str The main heading or subject of the blog post. content : str The complete textual content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A sanitized, HTML‑formatted string ready for rendering. Raises ------ TypeError If either argument is not a string. """ if not isinstance(headline, str): raise TypeError("headline must be a string") if not isinstance(content, str): raise TypeError("content must be a string") # Escape HTML special characters to prevent injection attacks. safe_title = html.escape(headline, quote=True) # For the body we escape but also preserve line breaks as
. escaped_body = html.escape(content, quote=True).replace("\n", "
\n") # Insert the sanitized parts into the template. formatted = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=escaped_body) return formatted.strip()
